title: India Open Asian Games Cricket Title Defence Against Hosts Japan
excerpt: Defending champions India face hosts Japan in the women's T20 quarter-final on September 18, opening the bid to retain both the men's and women's cricket gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
body:
• India's women's team opens its Asian Games title defence against hosts Japan in the quarter-final at Korogi Athletic Park on September 18, with the women's T20 tournament running September 17 to 22.
  • India are defending champions in both the men's and women's events after winning double gold at Hangzhou 2023.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur leads a 15-player women's squad with Smriti Mandhana as vice-captain; Shreyas Iyer captains the men's side, which plays its quarter-final on September 28.
  • India and Pakistan sit on opposite halves of the men's draw and can only meet in the semi-final or the final, according to the official schedule.

India's women begin the defence of their Asian Games cricket title on Thursday against hosts Japan, the first step in a campaign to retain the double gold the country won at Hangzhou in 2023. The quarter-final at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi Prefecture opens a straight-knockout women's T20 tournament that runs from September 17 to 22, two days before the Aichi-Nagoya Games officially open on September 19.

Japan, entering through the preliminary group stage, get the home draw and the crowd. India arrive as overwhelming favourites and one of only four seeded teams across the two tournaments, alongside Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. Every quarter-final is sudden death — one poor session with bat or ball ends the gold medal bid, according to tournament coverage of the draw.

Context & Background

Cricket returned to the Asian Games at Hangzhou 2023 in the T20 format with full international status, and India took both titles. Harmanpreet Kaur's side beat Sri Lanka in the women's final after overcoming Bangladesh in the semi-final, while the men, captained by Ruturaj Gaikwad, claimed the other gold. The women's squad named for Aichi-Nagoya largely resembles the group from that campaign: Harmanpreet leads, Smriti Mandhana is vice-captain, and senior players Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh and Renuka Singh all return. The one change sees wicketkeeper G. Kamalini come into the 15-player group, with all-rounder Shreyanka Patil included subject to fitness clearance after an ankle injury, per the ICC's squad announcement.

The format rewards pedigree but punishes complacency. The women's event is a straight knockout from the quarter-finals: India play Japan, with Bangladesh or China awaiting the winner in the semi-final on September 20, while Sri Lanka play Malaysia and Pakistan play Thailand in the other half of the draw. The men's tournament, featuring ten teams, begins with a six-team preliminary round from September 24, with Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal in Group A and Hong Kong, Malaysia and Oman in Group B. The four seeded sides join at the quarter-final stage. India's men play their quarter-final on September 28 against the Group A runner-up, with semi-finals on October 1 and the gold medal match on October 3, according to the official schedule.

"India has set a benchmark in Asian cricket over the years."

— Sanjay Manjrekar, former India cricketer

Impact & Analysis

The draw shape gives India a clear route but a high-stakes one. The women's side must win three consecutive knockout matches to repeat as champions, and a knockout bracket has no margin for the slow starts that group stages forgive. For Harmanpreet's squad, the Games also arrive with extra context: the team is coming off a group-stage exit from the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, and a gold in Japan would reset the narrative before the side regroups for the next World Cup cycle. India's automatic qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics — secured as the highest-ranked Asian team — is already banked, so Aichi-Nagoya is purely about prestige and momentum.

The men's draw has the subplot everyone noticed immediately. India and Pakistan sit on opposite halves of the knockout bracket, which means the arch-rivals can only meet in the semi-final or the final — if both survive their quarter-finals. Shreyas Iyer captains the men's side with Tilak Varma as deputy, and the squad includes teenage batting prospect Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, giving the defending champions a blend of experience and audacious youth, per schedule coverage.

Diaspora Angle

Cricket at a continental multi-sport event is a rare stage for the diaspora in Japan, where a small but growing cricket community gets a home-town encounter with the world's strongest side, while Asian diaspora fans across the region get a familiar festival of rivalry inside a Games that has moved beyond the Commonwealth spotlight.

What's Next

The women's quarter-final against Japan is scheduled for 2:00 PM Japan time on September 18. Win it, and India face Bangladesh or China in the semi-final on September 20; the bronze medal match and final follow on September 22. The men's preliminary round runs September 24 to 27, with India's quarter-final on September 28, semi-finals on October 1 and the final on October 3. Beyond Aichi-Nagoya, the double title defence doubles as an early benchmark in the road to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket returns to the Olympic programme.
